Hi Irene / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Pete and I are excited to kick off the two-week trial next week. I attached our completed vendor onboarding form (onyx_onboarding_form.pdf). One point from procurement on our side: our finance team typically requires a purchase order before any paid vendor activity. Given this is a short, low-risk trial (est. spend ~$2k), our procurement has asked whether Redwood can accept invoices without an initial PO and bill retrospectively after trial completion.

Can you confirm Redwood's stance on no-PO trial billing? If a formal exception is required, what documentation do you need from us and what approvals are typical on Redwood's side? We want to avoid blocking the start date.

Appreciate a quick note on options and any small-addendum you may require.

Thanks,
Laura Moss
Head of Procurement (Onboarding)
OnyxLabs

Hi Laura — great to hear, and thanks for the completed form. Attaching it to the onboarding record now.

Short answer: we prefer a PO for invoiced engagements, but we do have a documented temporary invoice path for small trials under limited conditions. To approve a no-PO invoice path we need: 1) the completed onboarding form (received), 2) procurement confirmation of estimated spend and that this is a one-off trial (can be via email), and 3) an approved risk check from our Finance runbook (I can initiate). On Redwood's side, approval typically comes from Procurement + Finance lead; legal signs a short addendum only if contract terms are altered.

Proposed conditional path for OnyxLabs trial:
- Trial spend cap: $5,000 total (covers your estimate)
- Billing: Redwood will invoice for trial usage within 7 days after trial close; net 30 payment term
- Evidence: we need a single email from your procurement agreeing to the budget cap and that this is trial-only
- Addendum: a short one-paragraph acknowledgment confirming no change to master terms (I can draft)

If you can confirm procurement's OK in a reply and attach any internal PO exceptions form they use, I will start the finance sign-off. If procurement requires a formal PO up front, we can also accept that — whichever gets you started faster.

Looping Karthik to confirm Finance constraints and Marissa for billing ops handoff.

Best,
Irene Choi
Vendor Operations — Procurement
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context, Irene. Laura — we can approve the temporary invoice path for this trial under the conditions Irene outlined plus a couple small safeguards from Finance:

1) Spend cap hard limit: $5,000 (no exceptions without prior written approval from Redwood Finance Director).
2) Single invoice after trial: Redwood will send one invoice covering trial usage; OnyxLabs agrees to Net 30.
3) Billing contact & remittance: please confirm who will receive invoices and process payments (name + email + billing address).
4) Evidence pack: please reply to this thread with a short line from your procurement (e.g., "OnyxLabs procurement confirms trial spend cap of $5,000 and accepts invoicing after trial"). That will be retained on the vendor file.

We don't typically require Legal to execute an addendum for trials of this size, but if your procurement team prefers a signed confirmation we can route a one-paragraph Temporary PO Addendum. I'll draft and send for signatures if needed.

Marissa — when this is confirmed by Onyx procurement, can you create a temporary billing lane (Vendor: OnyxLabs, flag: TEMP-INVOICE-TRIAL, retention: standard) and watch for the post-trial invoice? Also note: we will not enable auto-renew billing without a formal PO or order form.

Karthik
Director, Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference
